title: Enable userspace DHCP through generic Linux packet sockets
summary: Make the existing BusyBox udhcpc work through generic AF_PACKET, readiness, rtnetlink, and device paths without implementing DHCP in the kernel or embedding interface, address, topology, repository, or credential facts in production code.

in: per-network-namespace packet socket registration and close withdrawal
generic AF_PACKET SOCK_RAW and SOCK_DGRAM Ethernet transmit and receive semantics
AF_INET SOCK_RAW IPPROTO_RAW control-socket compatibility used by BusyBox interface ioctls
protocol and ifindex receive filtering with readiness publication
layer-2 ingress for interfaces that are up but have no IP address
BusyBox udhcpc control-plane compatibility through existing rtnetlink, ioctl, poll, and VFS paths
scenario-driven RV64 and LA64 QEMU DHCP witnesses
runsh Alpine /sbin overlay and parameterized public Git clone witness
deferred VF2 and unspecified LA real-board acceptance hooks
out: an in-kernel DHCP state machine or DHCP packet parser
DHCPv6, router advertisements, SLAAC, or an in-kernel DNS resolver
DWMAC, StarFive PHY, DMA, or IRQ implementation
a fabricated LA real-board profile before the board model is known
embedded proxies, Git remotes, credentials, CA material, or time policy
write_sets: docs/progress DHCP plan and status records

steps.title: Freeze the userspace DHCP and no-hardcoding contract
verification: The plan distinguishes kernel Linux ABI work from userspace DHCP protocol work.
Production-code prohibitions include process, port, interface, address, topology, repository, and credential special cases.
The baseline identifies fake AF_PACKET success, absent RX fanout, no packet registry, and no-address ingress starvation.
steps.notes: The local QEMU packet-socket slice is implementation-ready; hardware acceptance remains conditional on each board driver.

steps.title: Add per-namespace packet socket registration and lifecycle
verification: Packet sockets are registered only in their owning namespace.
Close withdraws the packet socket before payload retirement.
Capacity exhaustion is explicit and tested.
steps.notes: Use the existing raw-ICMP registry lifecycle as the local pattern.

steps.title: Fan out real device ingress to matching packet sockets
verification: SOCK_RAW receives a complete Ethernet frame and SOCK_DGRAM receives the payload.
Protocol, ETH_P_ALL, bound ifindex, unbound ifindex, namespace, and close filtering are covered.
One device receive feeds packet subscribers and normal L3 demux without competing drains.
An up interface with no IPv4 address still receives packet frames.
The first queued frame publishes receive readiness and wakes poll.
steps.notes: Each subscriber receives an independent copy; one full queue cannot block other consumers.

steps.title: Transmit packet socket data through the selected real net device
verification: SOCK_RAW transmits the caller's complete frame unchanged to a veth peer.
SOCK_DGRAM constructs the Ethernet header from namespace device and sockaddr_ll facts.
Invalid/down devices, malformed addresses, oversize frames, and busy devices return bounded errors.
The synthetic ARP self-reply production path is removed.
steps.notes: The syscall shim owns only user-copy and ABI translation; the net subsystem owns device semantics.

steps.title: Make DHCP-produced namespace and FIB state authoritative
verification: The BusyBox udhcpc script can replace address, route, and DNS state.
Ordinary TCP and UDP egress uses the current namespace address and FIB after replacement.
Static, DHCP, and none modes are external inputs and require no kernel rebuild.
steps.notes: The dhcp/none boot modes now leave address and route truth exclusively in the namespace and the boot delegate no longer owns a private EtherIface. The legacy static QEMU values remain as a compatibility default; moving those values into the external scenario renderer is still pending.

steps.title: Run a real RV64 QEMU BusyBox udhcpc witness
verification: QEMU network arguments are actually connected to the shell-test command.
A temporary copy of the Alpine ext4 image is used.
A fixture-provided non-default subnet produces a real udhcpc lease, route, DNS, and gateway ping.
The serial log contains native udhcpc output and stable DHCP sentinels.
steps.notes: The parameterized witness acquired 172.31.44.20 from a non-default fixture, reached its DHCP-provided gateway and DNS, then completed a TLS-verified shallow clone of the externally supplied public xv6 GitHub remote. Concrete values are fixture inputs only.

steps.title: Reuse the witness on LA64 QEMU and cover bounded failures
verification: LA64 QEMU passes the same guest DHCP ABI witness.
No-server, down-link, bad-ifindex, queue-full, and device-busy cases fail within the timeout ladder.
Changing subnet, device placement, registration order, and ifindex does not require source edits.
steps.notes: Do not weaken the RV64 witness or add architecture-specific DHCP logic.

steps.title: Attach the common DHCP witness to ready real-board drivers
verification: VF2 uses the common witness after DWMAC and StarFive support is ready.
The future LA board adds only its platform profile and driver resources.
No fictional LA target, controller value, address, or topology is introduced before hardware identification.
steps.notes: Hardware-dependent acceptance remains deferred, not silently skipped or claimed complete.

verification.command: focused tx-subsystems, tx-shims, and xtask packet/DHCP prerequisite tests
verification.notes: Packet registry 1/1, packet RX/TX 2/2, AF_PACKET syscall wire tests 3/3, AF_INET IPPROTO_RAW control socket 1/1, and shell-test rendering 5/5 passed.
Final RV64 QEMU doctor and kernel build passed; existing compiler warnings remain.
A non-default QEMU subnet produced a real BusyBox lease, DHCP gateway ping, DHCP DNS lookup, TLS-verified GitHub shallow clone, and guest HEAD f5dea58.
Workspace build passed. The existing tx-shims 37 failures and tx-kernel 3 failures remain (two init chmod assertions and the ThreadFuture size budget); the focused packet/DHCP tests pass.
The pre-existing 23 broken links and 6 stale-vocabulary warnings remain; neither new DHCP document is reported.
The global walk still stops at the pre-existing invalid completed step status in the 2026-07-24 network-time plan; this record passes jq structure and status assertions.

risks: Boot and namespace runtimes can compete for the same receive queue unless packet fanout is inserted at the actual single ingress owner.
Treating SOCK_DGRAM as SOCK_RAW breaks BusyBox udhcpc even when transmit reaches the device.
Skipping interfaces without IPv4 prevents the first DHCP offer from being observed.
Synthetic ARP behavior and the default QEMU lease can create false-positive witnesses.
Updating namespace configuration without removing boot-runtime private address and route truth leaves later TCP and Git traffic on stale values.
A plaintext GitHub credential exists in a local helper script and must never enter logs or test fixtures.
blockers: VF2 completion requires the separate DWMAC and StarFive hardware phase.
The real LA board acceptance requires the board model and firmware facts.
Full four-mode automatic networking still depends on portable-network Phase 6 removing private boot-network truth.
